text: And fearless minds climb soonest unto crowns.
plain: Nerve gets you to the top before talent does.

text:
For many men that stumble at the threshold
Are well foretold that danger lurks within.
plain: Hesitation at the door is often your instinct warning you. Listen to it.

text:
A little fire is quickly trodden out,
Which, being suffered, rivers cannot quench.
plain: Stamp out a small fire now, or no river will put it out later.

text:
Lo, now my glory smeared in dust and blood!
My parks, my walks, my manors that I had,
Even now forsake me; and of all my lands
Is nothing left me but my body’s length.
Why, what is pomp, rule, reign, but earth and dust?
And live we how we can, yet die we must.
plain: Power, land, and fame end as dust. You get to choose how you live, not whether you die.

text:
Great lords, wise men ne’er sit and wail their loss,
But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.
plain: Smart people skip the wailing and start fixing.

text: As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.
plain: Complaining to the waves changes nothing. Neither does asking nicely.

text:
Why, courage then! What cannot be avoided
’Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.
plain: What you can't avoid, you don't get to dread. Spend that energy on something else.

text: The harder matched, the greater victory.
plain: The harder the opponent, the bigger the win.

text:
Suspicion always haunts the guilty mind;
The thief doth fear each bush an officer.
plain: A guilty mind sees danger everywhere.

text:
This shoulder was ordained so thick to heave,
And heave it shall some weight or break my back.
plain: I'll carry the weight or break trying.

text:
To climb steep hills
Requires slow pace at first. Anger is like
A full hot horse, who being allowed his way,
Self-mettle tires him.
plain: Rushing and rage burn you out before you arrive. Anger wears out its own rider.

text:
Heat not a furnace for your foe so hot
That it do singe yourself. We may outrun
By violent swiftness that which we run at,
And lose by over-running.
plain: Make your enemy's fire too hot and you get burned. Too much speed loses the race.

text:
For our best act. If we shall stand still
In fear our motion will be mocked or carped at,
We should take root here where we sit,
Or sit state-statues only.
plain: Fear of criticism will root you in place like a statue.

text:
’Tis but the fate of place, and the rough brake
That virtue must go through.
plain: Being misjudged is the price of standing out.

text:
Things done well,
And with a care, exempt themselves from fear;
Things done without example, in their issue
Are to be feared.
plain: Done right and openly, there's nothing to fear. Done in the dark, expect trouble.

text:
Where you are liberal of your loves and counsels
Be sure you be not loose; for those you make friends
And give your hearts to, when they once perceive
The least rub in your fortunes, fall away
Like water from ye, never found again
But where they mean to sink ye.
plain: Be careful who you hand your heart to. Some friends vanish at the first crack in your luck.

text:
When I came hither, I was Lord High Constable
And Duke of Buckingham; now, poor Edward Bohun.
plain: Titles go. Stripped of them, you are just who you were.

text:
Farewell. And when you would say something that is sad,
Speak how I fell.
plain: If you must talk about my failure, tell it straight.

text:
Verily,
I swear, ’tis better to be lowly born
And range with humble livers in content
Than to be perked up in a glist’ring grief,
And wear a golden sorrow.
plain: Better to be humble and content than glittering and miserable.

text:
Our content
Is our best having.
plain: What you have, and being fine with it, is the best thing you own.

text:
Heaven is above all yet; there sits a judge
That no king can corrupt.
plain: No power on earth can bribe the final judge.

text:
I have touched the highest point of all my greatness,
And from that full meridian of my glory
I haste now to my setting. I shall fall
Like a bright exhalation in the evening,
And no man see me more.
plain: I peaked, and now I set like the sun. No one will see me again.

text:
This is the state of man: today he puts forth
The tender leaves of hopes; tomorrow blossoms,
And bears his blushing honours thick upon him;
The third day comes a frost, a killing frost,
And when he thinks, good easy man, full surely
His greatness is a-ripening, nips his root,
And then he falls, as I do.
plain: Hope blooms, honor piles up, then one frost kills the root. Greatness is never as safe as it feels.

text:
I have ventured,
Like little wanton boys that swim on bladders,
This many summers in a sea of glory,
But far beyond my depth.
plain: I swam in a sea of glory far past what I could handle.

text:
Vain pomp and glory of this world, I hate ye!
I feel my heart new opened. O, how wretched
Is that poor man that hangs on princes’ favours!
plain: Chasing a prince's favor is a miserable way to live.

text:
Never so truly happy, my good Cromwell.
I know myself now, and I feel within me
A peace above all earthly dignities,
A still and quiet conscience.
plain: Losing everything, he finally knows himself, and feels peace.

text:
Mark but my fall and that that ruined me.
Cromwell, I charge thee, fling away ambition!
By that sin fell the angels; how can man, then,
The image of his maker, hope to win by it?
Love thyself last; cherish those hearts that hate thee.
Corruption wins not more than honesty.
plain: Ambition ruined the angels. Honesty beats corruption in the end.

text:
Be just, and fear not.
Let all the ends thou aim’st at be thy country’s,
Thy God’s, and truth’s.
plain: Be fair, drop the fear, and aim at something bigger than yourself.

text:
Had I but served my God with half the zeal
I served my king, He would not in mine age
Have left me naked to mine enemies.
plain: Give your God the zeal you give your boss, or you'll be left naked when the boss drops you.

text: Press not a falling man too far! ’Tis virtue.
plain: Don't kick someone who's already down.

text:
Men’s evil manners live in brass; their virtues
We write in water.
plain: People remember your faults for good and your virtues for a day.

text:
His overthrow heaped happiness upon him,
For then, and not till then, he felt himself,
And found the blessedness of being little.
plain: Losing it all taught him who he was, and the peace of being small.

text:
O my good lord, that comfort comes too late;
’Tis like a pardon after execution.
plain: Comfort after it is too late is worth nothing.

text:
You take a precipice for no leap of danger,
And woo your own destruction.
plain: You think it's a harmless jump, but you are walking toward your own ruin.

text:
Leave me alone,
For I must think of that which company
Will not be friendly to.
plain: Some thoughts you can only think alone.

text:
Men that make
Envy and crooked malice nourishment
Dare bite the best.
plain: People fed on envy go after the best among us.

text:
Who dares not stir by day must walk by night,
And have is have, however men do catch.
Near or far off, well won is still well shot,
And I am I, howe’er I was begot.
plain: Whoever won't move in daylight must move at night. What you win is yours, however you came to it.

text:
Brother, take you my land, I’ll take my chance.
Your face hath got five hundred pound a year,
Yet sell your face for five pence and ’tis dear.
plain: Take the land. I'll take my chance on the world.

text: Out with it boldly. Truth loves open dealing.
plain: Say it plainly. The truth does not hide.

text: My father gave me honour, yours gave land.
plain: Some give you land. Better to be given honor.
